whatItIs.text: An ancient pulse eaten whole, ground into flour, or blended into hummus; kabuli (large, tan) is the usual Western type, desi (small, dark) the South Asian one.

historyNote.text: The chickpea is one of the earliest cultivated legumes, with the oldest archaeological evidence found in Syria; India alone grew three-quarters of the world's 2023 crop.

howToChoose.text: Canned, look for undented tins and firm whole beans; dried, choose even, uncracked grains and buy what you will use within a year for best cooking.

storage.text: Opened canned chickpeas go into a covered container in the fridge; dry ones live in an airtight jar in a cool cupboard. The rulebook has the timing.
storage.note: opened-can and cooked-pulse windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Leftover chickpeas crisp in a hot oven with oil and spice for snacks, mash into sandwich fillings, or stir into soups as a thickener.

substitutions.note: creamier and milder; blends smoother into dips
